ledger.sentence: 5-HT3 receptor antagonists are anti-sickness medicines; ondansetron is the member covered on this site.
ledger.note: NHS sheet: ondansetron is a 5HT3-receptor antagonist

ledger.sentence: Ondansetron is used to prevent nausea and vomiting after chemotherapy, radiotherapy and surgery.
They block 5-HT3 receptors for serotonin in the gut and the central nervous system.
It may be given by mouth as a tablet, melt or syrup, or as an injection into a vein, according to Great Ormond Street Hospital.
The MHRA has warned of a small increased risk of cleft lip or palate after first-trimester use of ondansetron.
A UK leaflet says ondansetron must not be used with apomorphine.
An NHS prescribing sheet says ondansetron lengthens the QT interval in a dose-related way and is avoided in congenital long QT syndrome.
